summary: Targeted backend-only RBAC verification of the CMS_WRITE permission fix for ADMINISTRATOR on GET/PUT /api/admin/settings/visuals. Extended /app/backend/tests/test_cms_visuals.py from 14 to 19 tests. All 19 PASS. Verified full RBAC matrix: SUPER_ADMIN GET+PUT=200, ADMINISTRATOR (adminr@azuris.local) GET=200 + PUT=200 [fix under test], CONTENT_MANAGER GET+PUT=200, CUSTOMER_SERVICE GET=200 + PUT=403, unauthenticated PUT=401. Audit trail verified via direct MongoDB query — audit_logs collection contains entries with entity_type='cms_visuals' after ADMINISTRATOR PUT. Regression guard: WhatsApp contact PUT /api/admin/settings — CONTENT_MANAGER=>403 and CUSTOMER_SERVICE=>403 remain unchanged, while ADMINISTRATOR still gets 200 (as required by require_roles(ADMINISTRATOR) guard). Baseline invariant confirmed: certificate_counter.last_number=14, next_number='AZR-GEM-000015-26'. Business collection totals in analytics.overview all 0.
critical_code_review_comments: auth/rbac.py: ADMINISTRATOR frozenset now includes both CMS_READ and CMS_WRITE — matches the required matrix and uses the existing permission architecture (no hardcoded role check).

api/settings.py: GET /admin/settings/visuals uses require_permission(CMS_READ); PUT uses require_permission(CMS_WRITE). Contact PUT /admin/settings correctly retains require_roles(ADMINISTRATOR) — CM/CS still 403.

No admin-facing audit-log query endpoint exists (audit is verified via Mongo). Not a blocker for this scope; consider a read-only /api/admin/audit-logs endpoint (SUPER_ADMIN, LOGS_READ) in a future iteration.
